pretreatments.description: Synthetic Food Waste (FW) preparation: Blending of various foods (fruits, vegetables, meat, rice, paste, and dairy products) to achieve homogenization. This process involves mechanical degradation of the food matrix, preparing the substrate for subsequent treatments.

Thermophilic Pretreatment (TPP): Mixing FW and inoculum, incubation at varying temperatures (50, 60, 70 and 80 °C) for a varying time (12, 24, 36 and 48 h). After each TPP, the temperature of the incubator was reduced to mesophilic (35 ± 2 °C) conditions. This involves a thermal treatment to accelerate the AD process.

Conventional Thermal Pretreatment (CTP): Heating only the FW without inoculum to 50–80 °C for 1.5 h. This involves a thermal treatment to improve hydrolysis, increase the biomethane production, and to achieve pasteurization.

Batch BMP experiments of FW: BMP tests were conducted in 1 L glass bottles at mesophilic (35 ± 2 °C) conditions with a substrate to inoculum (S/I) ratio of 0.5 gVS/gVS, following the BMP protocol described by Esposito et al. (2012).
